subject: genetics
question: **Type:** concept Mendel crossed pea plants that differed at two loci and found that the allele combinations in the offspring were shuffled freely. Which statement describes the law of independent assortment?

options.text: Alleles at different loci are transmitted to offspring independently of one another
The two alleles at a single locus separate during gamete formation
The phenotype of a heterozygote is an exact blend of the two parental phenotypes
Alleles at loci on the same chromosome are always transmitted together

explanation: Independent assortment holds that alleles at different loci are distributed to gametes independently, so a dihybrid produces the four gamete classes in equal proportions. B states the law of segregation, which concerns a single locus. C is blending inheritance, which Mendel's results ruled out. D describes complete linkage, which is broken whenever crossing over separates the loci.
